summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style biographical overview of Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom, covering her birth and succession, her marriage to Prince Albert, her long reign known as the Victorian era, her seclusion after Albert's death, her relationships with John Brown and Abdul Karim, and her death at Osborne House in January 1901. It also covers her journals, her jubilees, and her dealings with prime ministers Gladstone and Salisbury.
one_line: Biographical overview of Queen Victoria's birth, succession, 63-year reign, marriage to Albert, seclusion, and death in 1901.
key_facts: Victoria was born at 4.15 a.m. on 24 May 1819 at Kensington Palace in London.
Victoria died on Tuesday, 22 January 1901, at half past six in the evening, at the age of 81.
Victoria's reign of 63 years and seven months was longer than that of any of her predecessors and is known as the Victorian era.
Victoria became Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland on 20 June 1837.
On 1 May 1876, Victoria adopted the additional title of Empress of India.
Victoria married her first cousin, Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha, in 1840.
Victoria's Golden Jubilee in 1887 marked the fiftieth anniversary of her accession on 20 June with a banquet to which 50 kings and princes were invited.
On 23 June 1887, Victoria engaged Abdul Karim, who was soon promoted to "Munshi" and taught her Hindustani.
Victoria's father was Prince Edward, Duke of Kent and Strathearn, and her mother was Princess Victoria of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld.
On 17 March 1883, Victoria fell down some stairs at Windsor, which left her lame until July.
From July 1832 until just before her death, Victoria kept a detailed journal that eventually encompassed 122 volumes.
After the Indian Rebellion of 1857, the British East India Company was dissolved and Britain's Indian possessions were formally incorporated into the British Empire.
Victoria's nine children married into royal and noble families across the continent, earning her the sobriquet "the grandmother of Europe".
After Albert's death in 1861, Victoria plunged into deep mourning and avoided public appearances, which temporarily strengthened republicanism.
In 1889, during a stay in Biarritz, Victoria became the first reigning monarch from Britain to set foot in Spain.

entities.name: Queen Victoria
entities.role: Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland from 1837 until her death in 1901, subject of the note

entities.name: Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha
entities.role: Victoria's first cousin whom she married in 1840

entities.name: Prince Edward, Duke of Kent and Strathearn
entities.role: Victoria's father, fourth son of George III

entities.name: John Brown
entities.role: Victoria's devoted personal attendant, to whom she dedicated More Leaves from a Journal of a Life in the Highlands

entities.name: Abdul Karim
entities.role: Indian Muslim waiter promoted to Munshi who taught Victoria Hindustani and remained in her service until her death

entities.name: Sir Henry Ponsonby
entities.role: Victoria's private secretary who opposed publication of her biography of Brown

entities.name: Frederick Ponsonby
entities.role: Equerry, son of Sir Henry, who discovered the Munshi had lied about his parentage

entities.name: Lady Flora Hastings
entities.role: Lady-in-waiting to Victoria's mother whose 1839 illness was rumoured to be a pregnancy by Sir John Conroy

entities.name: Sir John Conroy
entities.role: Figure in the Kensington System whom Victoria hated, named in rumours about Lady Flora Hastings

entities.name: King Edward VII
entities.role: Victoria's son and successor, who initiated the House of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha

entities.name: Emperor Wilhelm II of Germany
entities.role: Victoria's eldest grandson, present at her deathbed

entities.name: Prince Henry of Battenberg
entities.role: Man whom Beatrice fell in love with and later married after Victoria was won around

entities.name: Gladstone
entities.role: Prime minister whose government Victoria thought was the worst she had ever had; she later recalled him and called him a half crazy old man

entities.name: Lord Salisbury
entities.role: Prime minister who replaced Gladstone in 1885 and whose party later defeated Gladstone's in an election

entities.name: General Gordon
entities.role: Military figure whose death at Khartoum Victoria blamed on Gladstone

entities.name: King William IV
entities.role: Victoria's uncle who distrusted the Duchess of Kent's capacity to be regent

entities.name: Duchess of Kent
entities.role: Victoria's mother who was to act as regent if William IV died while Victoria was a minor

entities.name: Princess Beatrice
entities.role: Victoria's youngest daughter, appointed literary executor, who edited and destroyed the original journals

entities.name: Leopold
entities.role: Victoria's uncle to whom she wrote about Albert, and her youngest son who died in Cannes

entities.name: Randall Davidson
entities.role: Dean of Windsor who advised Victoria against publishing her Brown biography

entities.name: Lord Elgin
entities.role: Viceroy of India to whom Frederick Ponsonby reported about the Munshi

entities.name: British East India Company
entities.role: Company that ruled much of India until it was dissolved after the Indian Rebellion of 1857

entities.name: Muslim Patriotic League
entities.role: Body that Victoria's family accused Abdul Karim of spying for

entities.name: House of Hanover
entities.role: Royal house of which Victoria was the last British monarch

entities.name: House of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha
entities.role: Royal house initiated by Edward VII, the line of his father

entities.name: Royal Horticultural Society
entities.role: Body whose gardens at Kensington Victoria agreed to visit

entities.name: Osborne House
entities.role: Isle of Wight residence where Victoria spent Christmas 1900 and where she died

entities.name: Windsor Castle
entities.role: Royal residence where Victoria fell down stairs in 1883

entities.name: Balmoral Castle
entities.role: Private Scottish estate acquired by Victoria and Albert in 1847

entities.name: Kensington Palace
entities.role: London palace where Victoria was born

entities.name: Biarritz
entities.role: Location of the 1889 stay during which Victoria crossed into Spain

entities.name: Buckingham Palace
entities.role: Palace on whose railings a protester posted a mocking notice in March 1864

entities.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
entities.role: Conflict after which the British East India Company was dissolved and India was incorporated into the Empire

entities.name: Boer War
entities.role: South African war that was unpopular in mainland Europe in 1900

entities.name: Victorian era
entities.role: Period of industrial, cultural, political, scientific and military change named after Victoria's reign

entities.name: More Leaves from a Journal of a Life in the Highlands
entities.role: 1884 sequel to Victoria's earlier book, published by her

entities.name: Turri
entities.role: Victoria's favourite pet Pomeranian, laid upon her deathbed as a last request
